channel.title: Filters on Best of AI
channel.description: Recent content in Filters on Best of AI

item.title: Aftershoot
item.description:
It reviews a large set of photos, flags the best frames, and groups duplicates. Users train personal editing profiles, and edits can be sent to Lightroom or Capture One. It also offers retouching and other tools.

It is a subscription product.

Imagen AI and Narrative Select are alternatives. Aftershoot suits photographers with high volume.

item.title: Imagen AI
item.description:
Photographers upload past edits to build a personal profile. Imagen then edits new shoots and returns adjustments to Lightroom or Photoshop. It also includes culling and cropping tools.

It is billed per photo or by plan.

Aftershoot and Lightroom presets are alternatives. Imagen suits photographers who edit thousands of images.

item.title: Photo Mechanic
item.description:
Photographers ingest cards, view previews at high speed, and tag picks. IPTC metadata editing and templates speed up captions. Photos then move to Lightroom or Photoshop for editing.

It is a paid product.

Adobe Bridge and Lightroom handle some of the same tasks. Photo Mechanic suits photo editors working under deadline.

item.title: Pic-Time
item.description:
Clients view and favorite photos in a branded gallery. Photographers set up print stores with lab fulfillment. Automation sends reminders to buy, and AI features help with face search and categories.

A free plan exists, with paid plans for more storage and features.

Pixieset and ShootProof are alternatives. Pic-Time suits wedding photographers who sell prints.

item.title: Pixieset
item.description:
Photographers upload photos to private galleries with download options and an online store. Studio Manager handles contracts, invoices, and scheduling. Free and paid plans differ in storage.

It suits solo and small studios.

Pic-Time and ShootProof are alternatives. Pixieset suits wedding photographers.

item.title: PixInsight
item.description:
It uses scripts and process modules for tasks like background extraction, noise reduction, and deconvolution. Add-ons use machine learning for noise and star removal. Photographers work in a non-destructive way and save workflows.

The interface is technical, and beginners usually take time to learn it. It is sold as a license.

Siril is a free alternative, and Photoshop is used for finishing. PixInsight suits serious astrophotographers.

item.title: Adobe Photoshop
item.description:
Photoshop is the image editor most photographers, retouchers, and designers learn first. It works on pixels in layers, with masks, selections, adjustment layers, and blend modes that let you change one part of an image without touching the rest. Photo retouching, product shots, poster layouts, and web graphics all fit into that same layer-based workflow, which is why files and techniques carry from one studio to the next.

The AI features sit inside that workflow instead of replacing it. Generative Fill takes a selection and a short text prompt and creates new content that matches the lighting and perspective around it. Generative Expand extends the canvas past the original edges, and the Remove tool erases distractions like power lines or stray people. Select Subject and Neural Filters handle selections, portrait adjustments, and colorization with less manual work. Generated content arrives on its own layer, so you can mask it, blend it, or throw it away.

item.title: Capture One
item.description:
Capture One began as software for tethered shooting, where a camera connects to a computer and photos appear on screen immediately, and it’s still a leader there. Studio and commercial photographers like its fast, reliable tethering, strong RAW processing, and color tools, including detailed color editing, skin tone adjustment, and support for many camera profiles. It offers a catalog system and sessions for organizing shoots.

Editing features include layers and masks, advanced color grading, and tools for sharpening and noise reduction. AI is used for masking, such as selecting subjects and backgrounds, and for other tasks that speed up workflow. A mobile app and live collaboration features let clients and teams review images during a shoot, and it works across Mac and Windows.

item.title: DxO PhotoLab
item.description:
DxO PhotoLab builds on years of lab testing of cameras and lenses. When you open a RAW file, it automatically applies corrections specific to your camera and lens combination for distortion, vignetting, and sharpness, which gives a solid starting point. The editor then provides tools for exposure, color, tone, and detail, with local adjustments using masks and control points inherited from the Nik Collection, which DxO owns.

Its noise reduction is its best-known feature. DeepPRIME XD uses AI to remove noise and recover detail from high-ISO images, and many photographers rate it among the best available, especially for low-light work. Other tools include ClearView for contrast, color rendering profiles, and lens sharpness adjustments. It works as a standalone editor and as a plugin with Lightroom or Photoshop, and DxO also sells PureRAW for batch processing.

item.title: GIMP
item.description: GIMP, the GNU Image Manipulation Program, has been a mainstay of free software for decades. It handles photo retouching, compositing, and digital painting with layers, masks, curves, selection tools, brushes, and a large set of filters. It reads and writes many file formats, including PSD files to a degree, and supports scripting in Python and Script-Fu for automation. The latest major version brought improvements such as non-destructive editing and better color management.

item.title: Perfect365
item.description:
Perfect365 started as a makeover app. A user takes or uploads a selfie, and face detection places virtual makeup, such as lipstick, eyeshadow, and foundation, or changes hair color. Retouching tools smooth skin and adjust features.

Salons and beauty professionals use virtual try-on to help clients picture a result, which supports decisions and sales. It is also popular for social media photos.

Heavy retouching can distort self-image, so use with care, and check the privacy policy since the app processes face photos. It is free with ads and paid options. Alternatives include YouCam Makeup, Facetune, FaceApp, and Modiface. Perfect365 suits casual users and beauty professionals.

item.title: Free AI Face Swap
item.description:
Free AI Face Swap lets a user upload two photos and exchange the faces. The tool detects faces, aligns them, and blends the result. It runs in the browser, supports common image formats, and offers extra effects around face editing.

People use face swaps for entertainment, memes, and creative projects. The same technology can be misused to create misleading or non-consensual images, so use only photos of people who have agreed, and never use swaps to deceive or harass. Many places have laws about deepfakes and intimate image abuse.

item.title: Let's Enhance
item.description:
Let’s Enhance takes a small or low-quality image and makes it larger. The AI adds plausible detail as it increases resolution, so a photo can be printed bigger or used on a high-resolution display with less blur. It also reduces noise and compression artifacts and improves color and lighting.

E-commerce sellers use it to improve product photos, designers to rescue old assets, and photographers to prepare prints. Batch processing and an API handle large volumes, and extra tools cover background removal and image generation.

item.title: Magnific AI
item.description:
Magnific is known as a creative upscaler. Where a standard upscaler sharpens existing pixels, Magnific uses generative AI to invent plausible detail, such as skin texture, fabric, foliage, and architectural elements, guided by a prompt and sliders for how much the image should change. The results can be striking, especially for AI-generated art.

The tool also supports style transfer, relighting, and other transformations, and its capabilities have been added to Freepik’s broader creative platform. Freepik acquired Magnific and kept it as a distinct brand, offering API access to its upscaling features.

item.title: Palette.fm
item.description:
Palette.fm adds color to old photos. A user uploads a black-and-white image, and the AI predicts plausible colors for skin, clothing, sky, and objects, returning a colorized version in seconds. Different style options change the overall palette, and results can be refined.

Families use it for old portraits, and historians and archivists use it to make collections more engaging. Colorization is an educated guess based on learned patterns, so colors may not match the real scene, and it should not be presented as historically accurate.

item.title: Perfect Corp
item.description:
Perfect Corp makes AI and augmented reality tools for beauty and fashion. Its skin analysis reads a selfie, scores concerns, and recommends products, while virtual try-on shows makeup, hair color, and accessories on the user’s face in real time.

Brands embed the technology in their websites, apps, and in-store screens to help shoppers choose and reduce returns. Clinics use simulations to show likely effects of treatments. The company also owns the YouCam consumer apps.

item.title: Adobe Lightroom AI
item.description:
Lightroom is built for photographers who handle many images. It organizes a library, lets you rate and filter, and edits photos non-destructively with sliders for exposure, color, tone, and detail. Edits can be copied across a whole shoot, which saves hours after a wedding or event. Lightroom syncs between desktop, phone, and the web, while Lightroom Classic is the desktop-only version with a more traditional file-based workflow.

AI has changed the way people edit in it. Masking tools select the subject, sky, background, or people with a click, so you can adjust one part of a photo without painting a selection. Denoise cleans up high-ISO images while preserving detail, Generative Remove deletes distractions, and Lens Blur adds realistic background blur. Adaptive presets adjust to the content of each photo, and auto-edit settings give a starting point.

item.title: BeFunky
item.description:
BeFunky is a browser-based editor for people who want quick results without learning Photoshop. The photo editor has sliders for exposure and color, crop and resize tools, and a large set of filters and effects. A collage maker arranges photos into layouts, and the graphic designer tool offers templates for social media posts, flyers, and cards. Everything runs in a web page, with mobile access too.

AI tools handle common edits. An enhancer sharpens and improves photos, a background remover cuts out subjects, and retouching tools smooth skin and remove blemishes. Artistic effects turn photos into paintings or cartoons, and an upscaler increases resolution. Newer features add AI image generation and a way to remove objects. Many of these are one-click operations, which is the main appeal.

item.title: Cleanup.pictures
item.description:
Cleanup.pictures does one thing with minimal effort. Upload a photo, brush over a stranger in the background, a power line, a logo, or a blemish, and the tool removes it and fills the gap with a plausible background. Results come back within seconds and can be downloaded, which makes it a quick fix for product photos, real estate listings, travel pictures, and social media posts.

It works well on simple backgrounds such as sky, grass, walls, and water, and less well when the removed object sits in front of detailed patterns, faces, or text that the model would have to invent. For larger images, a higher-resolution output is available on paid plans. The same kind of inpainting appears in other tools, including Clipdrop, which offers a related cleanup feature, along with Photoshop’s Generative Fill and Remove tool and the Magic Eraser on Google Pixel phones.

item.title: Lensa AI
item.description:
Lensa is a mobile photo editor best known for a single viral feature. Magic Avatars let users upload a set of selfies and receive a collection of stylized portraits in the style of fantasy art, anime, or illustration. The effect spread quickly on social media, driving downloads and making many people aware of AI image generation. The avatars are created with a model fine-tuned on each user’s photos.

The core of the app is a selfie and portrait editor. It offers retouching for skin and eyes, background replacement, blur and sharpening, and a range of filters and effects. Subscribers get access to the full tool set, and Magic Avatars can be purchased as packs. Prisma Labs, the developer, also makes other photo and AI apps.

item.title: Neural.love
item.description:
Neural.love combines creation and repair tools in one web app. The generator creates images from text prompts with a choice of models and styles, while the enhancement tools improve existing pictures. Upscaling increases resolution, denoising cleans grainy photos, and restoration repairs scratches and faded color on old family pictures. Face enhancement can sharpen portraits, and colorization adds color to black-and-white images.

The platform is practical for photographers, genealogists, designers, and anyone with old or low-quality images. Users upload a file, choose the effect, and download the result, with credits consumed by each operation. An API lets developers add enhancement features to their own apps, and batch options handle many images. Generated images can be used in marketing and design, subject to the terms for each plan.

item.title: ON1 Photo AI
item.description:
ON1 Photo AI aims to shorten the path from a raw photo to a finished image. It analyzes a picture and suggests adjustments, then applies tools such as NoNoise AI for removing grain, Sharpener AI for restoring detail, and Super Resolution for enlarging photos. Other tools handle sky replacement, background removal, portrait retouching, and object removal, and automatic masking selects subjects, skies, and other regions for local edits.

It fits into several workflows. It can open and process RAW files directly, work as a standalone app, or run as a plugin inside Lightroom, Photoshop, and other editors, which lets photographers use its AI tools without leaving their usual software. Presets provide quick looks, and batch processing handles many images at once. A separate ON1 Photo RAW product adds organizing and layer-based editing.

item.title: Picsart AI
item.description:
Picsart began as a mobile photo editor and grew into a broad creative suite. Users edit photos with filters, collages, stickers, and text, make videos, and design social posts from templates. A community lets people share and remix content, which helped it spread among younger creators and small businesses.

AI is now central. Tools generate images from prompts, remove backgrounds and objects, expand pictures, replace elements, enhance and upscale photos, and create stylized avatars. Text-to-video and animation tools turn ideas into clips, and an AI writer helps with captions. Picsart also provides APIs and plugins so other platforms can use its image tools, and teams can use brand kits and shared workspaces.

item.title: Pixelcut
item.description:
Pixelcut focuses on product images. A seller photographs an item, removes the background in one tap, and places the product on a clean or styled backdrop. AI can generate scenes that suit a product, add shadows, and upscale low-resolution pictures.

Batch tools process many images, and templates help create ads, social posts, and listing graphics. The mobile app is popular with small sellers who shoot products with a phone.

Pixelcut has a free tier and paid plans. AI-generated scenes should still show the product accurately to avoid returns. Alternatives include Photoroom, Canva, Pebblely, Remove.bg, and Adobe Express. Pixelcut suits small online sellers.

item.title: Remini
item.description:
Remini gained a following for photo restoration. A user uploads an old family photo or a blurry picture, and the AI sharpens it, repairs damage, and enhances faces. It can also upscale images and colorize black-and-white ones.

The app expanded into AI-generated portraits and avatars from selfies, which went viral at times. Video enhancement is also offered. It runs mainly on phones, with processing in the cloud.

Remini has a free tier with ads and limits, and paid plans, and has faced criticism over subscription practices. Enhancement invents plausible detail, so faces may change from the original. Photos are uploaded, so check the privacy policy. Alternatives include Topaz Photo AI, Let’s Enhance, Photoshop’s neural filters, VanceAI, and Palette.fm. Remini suits people restoring family photos.

item.title: Topaz Photo AI
item.description:
Topaz Photo AI aims to fix the technical flaws in photos with little effort. When you open an image, it analyzes the content and suggests corrections, using models for noise reduction, sharpening, and increasing resolution. It handles problems like grainy high-ISO shots, soft focus, and motion blur, and can enlarge photos while adding believable detail. Many wildlife, sports, and event photographers use it to rescue difficult images.

The tool also offers face recovery, light adjustment, color balance, and a way to apply different adjustments to selected subjects. It can be run as a standalone application, as an external editor from Lightroom, or as a plugin for Photoshop, and processes batches of images. Models run locally on your computer and benefit from a good graphics card.

item.title: Upscayl
item.description: Upscayl makes AI upscaling available to anyone. You drag in a low-resolution image, choose a model, and the app enlarges it by two, three, or four times with added detail, saving the result to your computer. It includes models tuned for general photos, digital art, and sharpening, and supports batch processing for many files. Because it runs on your own hardware, there is no per-image fee, and your images stay private.

item.title: Vectorizer.ai
item.description:
Vectorizer.ai converts bitmap images into vectors, which are scalable files used for logos, print, and cutting machines. Upload a low-resolution logo or illustration, and the service traces the shapes into paths and fills, returning an SVG, EPS, PDF, or DXF that can be resized without losing sharpness. The AI approach produces cleaner curves and fewer stray points than older tracing tools, with controls to adjust the level of detail.

Designers use it to recover logos from low-quality files, sign makers and crafters use it to prepare artwork for vinyl cutters and laser engravers, and developers add it to workflows through an API. It handles flat-color artwork best, such as logos and icons, and it works less well on photographs, which turn into complex tracings with many shapes. A preview lets you see the result before paying.

item.title: Magnific AI
item.description:
Magnific AI takes a low-resolution image and produces a larger version with added, invented detail. Users control how much creative freedom the AI takes with settings such as creativity and resemblance, and can add a prompt describing what the detail should look like. This makes it different from conventional upscalers.

Artists use it to polish AI-generated images and to turn rough concept art into detailed illustrations. Designers use it to prepare images for large formats. The company was acquired by Freepik, and the technology is available through Magnific’s own site and Freepik’s tools.

item.title: BestPhotoAI
item.description:
BestPhotoAI is meant for fast photo improvement. A user uploads an image, and the tool can sharpen details, increase resolution, fix lighting and color, and retouch skin, then returns an enhanced version. The aim is to save time compared with manual editing in Photoshop or Lightroom.

Typical users are e-commerce sellers who need clean product photos, creators preparing profile and social images, and people restoring older pictures. Automated enhancement works best on ordinary issues like low light or noise, and results vary with the source image.

item.title: Fotor
item.description:
Fotor covers everyday editing for people who do not want Photoshop. In the photo editor, you crop, adjust color and light, apply filters and effects, and retouch portraits by smoothing skin and removing blemishes. A collage maker and a design studio offer templates for social posts, posters, and cards. Everything works in a browser, with matching apps for phones and computers.

AI tools handle the harder steps. One-click enhancement improves exposure and sharpness, background removal makes cutouts, an object remover erases distractions, and an upscaler enlarges small pictures. Newer features include text-to-image generation, avatars, and generative fill for extending or changing parts of an image. Fotor also has an AI video editor for simple clips.

item.title: Luminar Neo
item.description: Luminar Neo is built for photographers who want strong results without a lot of manual work. Instead of slider-heavy workflows, it offers AI tools that do the hard parts in a click. Sky AI replaces or enhances skies, Relight AI changes the lighting in a scene using depth information, Portrait Bokeh AI creates background blur, and tools for skin, face, and body adjustments handle portraits. Generative tools can erase objects and expand the canvas.

item.title: Photoroom
item.description:
Photoroom grew from a background remover into a full product photography tool. Take a picture of a product on a table, and the app cuts it out cleanly, then places it on a white background, a color, or an AI-generated scene with realistic shadows and lighting. For small sellers on marketplaces like Etsy, eBay, and Shopify, that means professional-looking listings without a studio.

Other features expand the range. An AI backgrounds tool creates settings from a text description, an instant shadow and relight tool adds depth, and a magic retouch removes objects and blemishes. Templates in standard sizes speed up posts for social media and marketplaces. Batch editing handles whole catalogs, and an API lets platforms add the same processing to their own apps. Teams can share brand templates.

item.title: Pixlr
item.description:
Pixlr offers editing in a browser without installing software. Pixlr E is a more advanced editor with layers, masks, and adjustment tools that resemble Photoshop, while Pixlr X is a simpler editor for quick fixes, collages, and templates. It opens common image formats, including PSD files to an extent, and works on desktop and mobile browsers.

AI features handle the hard parts. Background removal makes cutouts in a click, an object eraser removes distractions, generative fill and expand add or extend content from a prompt, and automatic enhancement and retouching improve photos. An AI image generator and tools for creating designs from templates broaden what it can do. Pixlr is part of the Inmagine group, which also offers stock content.
